reading.body:
H.R. 9183 is a one-party bill: Don Beyer sponsors it and all 21 recorded cosponsors are Democrats. The bill's own text is tagged to energy and data centers, which places it in the same territory as state and local rules on where AI compute may be built and who pays for its power. One lobbying filing names the bill, from ARM INC, and a filing that names a bill shows only that the bill was an issue in the lobbying, not the position taken on it.

The useful signal is the subject matter, not the vote count. A bill tagged to energy and data centers is a federal move into the siting and power question that currently runs through state and local law. That question is the binding constraint on AI scaling, because compute depends on buildings and power, and power depends on where regulators allow load to connect.

The data does not say what the bill would do, whether it has moved past introduction, or how the ARM filing relates to it. It records a sponsor, cosponsors, issue tags, and one filing. It does not cover committee action, hearings, or opposition, so no conclusion about the bill's prospects follows from it.
